title: The Sermon on the Mount
note: Matthew 5 to 7 gathers Jesus' best-known teaching into one sermon on a mountain: the Beatitudes, a deeper reading of the law, the Lord's Prayer, trust instead of worry, the Golden Rule, and the call to build on his words. Luke 6 has a shorter, similar 'Sermon on the Plain.'

src.t: Matthew 6:5-15, King James Version, Project Gutenberg eBook #10

read.title: On prayer (Matthew 6:5-15)
text: And when thou prayest, thou shalt not be as the hypocrites are: for they love to pray standing in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward. But thou, when thou prayest, enter into thy closet, and when thou hast shut thy door, pray to thy Father which is in secret; and thy Father which seeth in secret shall reward thee openly. But when ye pray, use not vain repetitions, as the heathen do: for they think that they shall be heard for their much speaking. Be not ye therefore like unto them: for your Father knoweth what things ye have need of, before ye ask him.

After this manner therefore pray ye: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come, Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil: For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.
For if ye forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you: But if ye forgive not men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.

q.q: Where does Jesus tell his hearers to pray?
o: In thy closet, with the door shut
At the corners of the streets

q.q: What should they not use, as the heathen do?
What happens if they do not forgive others their trespasses?
o: Neither will the Father forgive theirs
